{"id": "23223ee6-e075-4cbd-ace1-068630354d35", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I don't have a way to open or parse pcap/pcapng files directly — I don't have a packet-capture analysis tool in this session, so I can't dig into the capture itself.

What I *can* do is investigate the hang from the AWS side, if `10.0.2.20` is a resource in your environment. That usually turns up the same answer a packet trace would (e.g., SYN with no SYN-ACK = security group/NACL drop; SYN-ACK but no data = app-level stall on the server).

To do that I'd want to know:
- Is `10.0.2.20` an EC2 instance, load balancer, or something else, and in which account/region?
